licenses.note: The port recreates JEI's item list and carries the reference's MIT notice; JEI's own LICENSE.txt covers the name and the drawing it recreates.

licenses.note: The reference, JEI 18.0.0.66 for 1.20.6, is MIT (Copyright (c) 2014-2015 mezz). The commit is the last of the 1.20.6 line, 20 commits past the v18.0.0 tag, and the published 18.0.0.66 build lists it as its newest change.

deviations.what: The list is not drawn on a grug mod's own container screens; it is drawn on the player's inventory and on every other container screen, vanilla or another mod's, that is not a GrugScreen.
deviations.why: The first version targets the screens the issue names, and drawing on a mod's own GrugScreen would change that mod's GUI goldens. JEI draws its list on every container screen.

deviations.what: The list is paged with the back and next buttons, which are drawn as plain highlight boxes without the reference's arrows or page number.
deviations.why: The buttons' look is part of the chrome the first version does not draw.

deviations.what: There is no search box, so the list cannot be filtered.
deviations.why: Text input is not in the overlay API and a test run has no way to type into a screen; item names are not exposed either.

deviations.what: Ctrl+O hides and shows the overlay. The key is fixed and cannot be rebound, and the list is hidden entirely, where JEI keeps drawing its config button while its list is hidden.
deviations.why: The host has no key binding or config API for a mod to register a rebindable key.

deviations.what: Right-clicking an item does not open its uses or recipes, and there are no recipe categories or recipe screen.
deviations.why: The recipe viewer's category, uses and recipes host API is a separate piece of work.

deviations.what: There are no bookmarks, so an item cannot be pinned across screens.
deviations.why: Bookmarks need per-player persistent state, drag input and a second list beside the ingredient list.

deviations.what: There is no plugin API for other mods to register categories or ingredient subtypes, and no configuration screen or file for the mod's options.
deviations.why: A grug mod has no plugin boundary to extend and no configuration file it reads; what a grug mod may extend is a design question.

deviations.what: The items are ordered by registry key on 1.20.6, with the minecraft namespace first and everything else alphabetically, and by numeric item id on 1.2.5, Beta and Alpha, which have no registry key; JEI orders by creative tab and then by mod name. The same item therefore sits at a different place.
deviations.why: A stable key order is what a committed golden needs, and the host exposes no creative tabs; the older versions only have the numeric id, so that is the order they use. JEI's order is recorded as the difference.

deviations.what: The list is one entry per registered item except air, where JEI lists the stacks of the creative tabs: a potion, a splash potion and a lingering potion are separate entries there, and an op-only tab hides its items from a player who may not use them. The potion, splash and lingering variants are therefore missing from the port, and barrier, command block and the other op-only items are listed to every player.
deviations.why: The host exposes one Item per registry key and no creative-tab stacks, ingredient subtypes or per-player tab permissions; listing those stacks is a change to the item list itself.

deviations.what: Hovering an item draws the reference's highlight but no tooltip, item count or mod name, and the grid draws no search bar or button.
deviations.why: The overlay API has no tooltip callback or item-name source, and the first version draws no chrome beyond the icons and the highlight.

deviations.what: The port gives one item on a left or right click, a stack on shift+left or the middle button, and deletes the item on the cursor on a left click while it carries one. It has no give-versus-cheat mode and no cheat permission check, and the give plays no pickup sound and sends no "Gave ... to ..." chat message. A left click deletes whatever the cursor carries, where the reference gives one item instead when the carried stack can stack with the clicked one.
deviations.why: The overlay host exposes the press's button and whether shift is held, but not JEI's GiveMode setting, its cheat permission, its pickup sound, its chat line or the cursor stack's count and damage, which are a separate piece.

deviations.what: The item on the cursor is deleted where the reference deletes it, but on a client of a remote server the delete clears only that client's copy of the cursor, while the reference's packet removes the stack the server holds. The give is the half that does reach the server: a client joined to one names the item to it, which puts it in the player's inventory there (#1099).
deviations.why: The cursor a click reads and the delete it makes are calls of the overlay host on the client that draws it, and that client sends the server no cursor write, where the reference's delete packet does. The give had the same gap and now names the item to the server over the test-control channel.
